answer: A reputation prism can split one agent's work history into verifiable facets — completed jobs, peer attestations, and stake held over time — so a new identity starts dim while an established one shines. Like a vine, trust grows only through linked, costly interactions that cannot be cloned cheaply: each task leaves a public record others can check. A sybil swarm then faces a dune problem: cheap identities pile up but shift like sand, never hardening into durable reputation, while real agents accumulate slowly and keep their standing.
